Democrats have taken full control of the U.S. Congress in a massive
repudiation of Donald Trump's authoritarian presidency and his gross
mishandling of the economy.

The blue wave that observers have projected for months ended up being [a blue
tsunami](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democrats-capture-
full-control-congress-nbc-news-projects-fueled-victo-rcna607042) Tuesday
night. Democrats are expected to win a significant majority in the House of
Representatives, and they've already flipped seven Senate seats held by
Republicans.

For the first two years of Trump's second term, Republicans have held a
governing trifecta, denying Democrats much opportunity to block their agenda
or hold the president and his corrupt administration accountable. That's about
to change: With control of the House and Senate, Democrats will be able launch
formal investigations, and the president will no longer be able to ram through
legislation.

"We'll work with the Democrats," Trump told [the
](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/us/politics/trump-midterm-election-
results.html)_[New York
Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/us/politics/trump-midterm-election-
results.html)_ Tuesday evening. The president even claimed he'll accept the
election results. On Fox, meanwhile, Trump
[said](https://x.com/justinbaragona/status/2117845820758454392): "I have the
power of veto."

Democrats won GOP seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South
Carolina, and Texas. Former Governor Roy Cooper has long been expected to win
North Carolina. The other states were mostly considered toss-ups, or thought
to lean Republican.

Kansas [elected](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/adam-hamilton-
kansas-senate-democrat-winner-upset-roger-marshall-rcna603310) its first
Democratic senator since 1932, as Methodist minister Adam Hamilton beat GOP
Senator Roger Marshall.

In Ohio, former Senator Sherrod Brown, who lost his seat in 2024,
[regained](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/03/sherrod-brown-jon-
husted-ohio-senate) a place in Congress by beating Senator Jon Husted.

Texas state Rep. James Talarico easily
[defeated](https://apnews.com/article/texas-senate-talarico-paxton-midterm-
election-66df71a7c2bfa962cffd4134ef1a0364) scandal-plagued Attorney General
Ken Paxton, the first time Democrats have won a Senate seat in the Lone Star
State sine 1988.

In South Carolina, which had not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since
1998, Annie Andrews
[defeated](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/03/g-s1-151666/south-carolina-senate-
race-andrews-graham) Republican Senator Darline Graham. At Trump's urging,
Graham was appointed to the seat in July following the death of her brother
Lindsey Graham, the prominent Trump ally and long-serving GOP senator. It was
Lindsey Graham, of course, who furiously lobbied the president to launch the
U.S.-Israeli war in Iran - a decision that likely cost Republicans control of
Congress.

In Iowa, state Rep. Josh Turek,
[defeated](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/josh-turek-
democrats-iowa-senate-flip-democrats-majority-boost-hinson-rcna603305)
Republican Congresswoman Ashley Hinson - securing the majority for Democrats.

Dems quickly built on that majority in Maine, with five-term GOP Senator Susan
Collins reportedly [conceding](https://x.com/Acyn/status/2117848927374553371)
to Troy Jackson, the former state senate president. Jackson became the nominee
this summer after Graham Platner was forced to drop out.

Democrats also held onto the Senate seat in Minnesota, with Lieutenant
Governor Peggy Flanagan
[projected](https://www.washingtonpost.com/elections/results/2026/11/03/minnesota-
senate-flanagan-tafoya-live-updates/) as the winner against former NFL
sideline reporter Michele Tafoya

Dems could still expand their Senate majority. Results are still coming in
from Michigan, and polls only just closed in part of Alaska.
